target_customer: Pharma partners and investors funding neurodegenerative drug programs; since 2026 drug developers who buy data and target insights.
problem: Drug discovery for neurodegenerative diseases such as ALS fails often; Verge used human tissue genomics and machine learning to pick targets and drug candidates.
business_model: Venture funded drug discovery with pharma partnerships; from 2026 data and insights licensing

founders.name: Alice Zhang
founders.background_notes: YC page and press releases name her as the only founder and give no education or employers; BioPharma Dive calls her CEO and founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining proprietary human tissue genomics, machine learning target discovery and medicinal chemistry into clinical candidates is research grade.

defensibility.rationale: A proprietary patient tissue genomics dataset is a real asset, but drug candidates carry clinical risk and the field had many AI drug discovery entrants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pharma partnered rather than copied; Lilly signed a deal in July 2021 and joined the Series B, and Merck's venture arm invested.

market_need_then: ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases had very high clinical failure rates and unmet need, motivating human genomics based target discovery.

branding.domain_note: vergegenomics.com now redirects to vergelabs.com per a 301 redirect seen when fetched.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific, positioning around all in human data

branding.brand_signature: All in human data and the CONVERGE platform name

rebrands.why: After dropping its clinical asset and cutting about 90 percent of staff, it became a data and insights company per BioPharma Dive (May 27, 2026)

brand_strength.rationale: Fierce 15 recognition and strong trade press coverage, but no mascot or community; the genomics name was dropped in the 2026 pivot.

pivots.from: Own AI designed clinical pipeline for ALS and neurology
pivots.to: Verge Labs, monetizing datasets and insights for drug developers, with a spun out AI models company
pivots.why: Lead drug VRG50635 early trial did not help the intended patients; neurofilament light chain rose

outcome_analysis: Verge raised a 32 million dollar Series A in 2018 and a 98 million dollar Series B in December 2021 backed by BlackRock, Lilly and Merck, and signed a Lilly deal worth up to 706 million dollars reported in 2021. Its lead ALS drug failed an early trial that ended in December 2025, after which it cut about 90 percent of staff and rebranded as Verge Labs in 2026, so it stalled on the clinical bet though it still operates.
